title: SoftBank weighs $30 billion Allied Universal deal as Son eyes security robots
source_used: Investing.com text on Yahoo Finance (relay of Bloomberg); Bloomberg itself is behind a robot check
key_facts: Bloomberg reported on Friday 16 Oct 2026, citing people familiar with the matter, that SoftBank Group is considering buying Allied Universal, the largest security services company in the US.
The closely held company could be valued at up to $18 billion in equity; with about $12 billion of publicly traded debt the total deal value could be close to $30 billion.
Discussions are preliminary and no final decisions have been made on a deal or its price.
SoftBank founder Masayoshi Son sees security as a promising area for robots, with fleets possibly replacing human guards at one-off events such as concerts when the economics work.

Allied Universal provides guards for businesses, events and infrastructure, including New York City's subway under contracts with the Metropolitan Transportation Authority, and has a significant presence in security for data center building.
Investing.com notes that complex security work, emergency response and jobs needing human judgment may stay hard to automate.
quote_evidence: Discussions remain preliminary, and no final decisions have been made on a deal or its price.

The closely held security company could be valued at as much as $18 billion in equity, while its roughly $12 billion in publicly traded debt could bring the total transaction value close to $30 billion, according to Bloomberg.

Son has identified security as a promising area for robotics deployment, with fleets of robots potentially replacing human guards at one-off events such as concerts when the economics make sense, Bloomberg reported.
why_it_matters_hint: A big SoftBank bet on physical AI would use a huge security workforce as a place to test robots, but talks are early.
notes: Same story as C11-05 (Bloomberg, also Reuters citing Bloomberg). Bloomberg text blocked; read the Investing.com copy on Yahoo Finance, which credits Bloomberg. Reuters headline puts the figure at $18 billion (equity); Investing.com adds the debt to reach about $30 billion.
